source.check: returned unopposed: 'There are eleven unopposed returns to Derry Rural Council. Two seats are being contested - Claudy ... and the Middle Liberties' (Derry Journal 23 May 1958 p7, image read), which names each unopposed member with the division. The paper prints his townland in place of the division.

note: Triennial election of the rural district councillors, polled Thursday 5 June 1958. Two contests, Claudy and Middle Liberties (Belfast News-Letter, 6 June 1958, p. 5; Irish News, 6 June 1958, p. 1). The eleven unopposed members added from the Derry Journal, 23 May 1958, p. 7, which names each with the division (Upper Liberties printed as his townland) (round-2 gap-fill, 7 Nov 2026). division inferred from the 2 June 1955 return (James Mackey, Liberties (Upper); Returning Officer's notice, Derry Journal, 6 June 1955, p. 5); the Derry Journal of 23 May 1958, p. 7, names the member as returned unopposed. Returned unopposed.
correctionNote: Renamed from 'Upper Liberties' to Liberties Upper (13 Nov 2026, by the owner's rule for division spellings: the official or DED-map name where there is one, otherwise the spelling most rounds use): the DED maps of 1930-69 (LIBERTIES UPPER) spell it Liberties Upper. This round was filed under the spelling 'Upper Liberties', a form of the division's name it keeps as an alias; the old address (upper-liberties) answers with a redirect to this one.
